## Overview

SwingOS is a real-time computer vision tool that watches a baseball swing through a webcam and gives instant feedback on head movement — one of the most common mechanical breakdowns in hitting. I built it to see if I could train my body to feel correct mechanics without needing a coach standing there watching every rep.

**Stack:** Python, OpenCV, MediaPipe

## How It Works

MediaPipe's pretrained pose-landmark model tracks 33 body landmarks per frame in real time. The app pulls out just the nose landmark as a proxy for head position, lets the user lock in an anchor point (`S` key), and then continuously compares the live head position against that anchor.

```python
if key == ord('s'):
    if results.pose_landmarks:
        nose = results.pose_landmarks.landmark[mp_pose.PoseLandmark.NOSE]
        head_anchor_y = nose.y
        status = "ANCHOR SET - STAY LEVEL"

if head_anchor_y is not None:
    current_nose_y = results.pose_landmarks.landmark[mp_pose.PoseLandmark.NOSE].y
    diff = int(head_anchor_y * h) - int(current_nose_y * h)
    if abs(diff) > 20:
        status = "WATCH YOUR HEAD!" if diff < 0 else "STAY DOWN!"
    else:
        status = "SOLID"
```

A green line marks the anchor, a red line marks the current head position, and a status banner tells the hitter to adjust in real time — no delay, no reviewing footage after the fact.

## Why It Matters

This is applied ML in the sense that matters to me most: taking a general-purpose pretrained model (pose estimation) and wiring it into a tight feedback loop that solves a specific, real problem. The interesting part isn't training a model — it's turning model output into a signal a person can actually act on in the half-second it takes to swing a bat.
